t: You're standing near the site of Baynard's Castle, between where Blackfriars station and St Paul's Cathedral now stand. There were two buildings here. The first was a Norman fortification built by Ralph Baynard and demolished by King John in 1213. The second was a medieval palace, built a little to the south-east and later extended, which was mostly destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666. Algernon Sidney, the republican political theorist later executed for treason, was born here. So was Philip Sidney, the 3rd Earl of Leicester, and Anne Herbert, Countess of Pembroke, sister of Catherine Parr, died here.
